answer: A robust defense is hardware-bound identity: each agent must present a fresh attestation from a real secure enclave, signed by its device key, before the network admits it. A cipher signature proves the enclave is genuine, and one device can only vouch for a handful of agents, so a sybil farm lands in a shallow hollow: it can spawn identities cheaply, but without real hardware backing they never float. In an ocean of ephemeral processes, hardware attestation makes each participant a verifiable, scarce body.
